newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, marks to rise further.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, marks to rise further.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, with the key contracts finishing higher, as Mexican pesos and sterling closed sharply lower.
September marks continued to find upside momentum above resistance at $0.5361, or 1.87 spot, and are expected to grind higher in the near term, traders and floor analysts said.

Options on futures contracts implied to several currency traders that September marks were preparing to stage a corrective rally. One French-based firm bought 1,100 September mark calls at a strike price of $0.5500, while one U.S. firm sold 1,000 December mark puts with strikes at $0.4800.
"If those aren't hedges, then they are looking for an upward move," one currency futures floor analyst said.
There were also rumors that one prominent hedge fund manager based in Chicago was preparing to sell dollars and dollar-denominated assets, and buy foreign currencies.
Traders said technicals alone called for an upswing in marks futures and cash marks against most European currencies.
Another floor trader expects September marks to rally to $0.5442 or 1.8420 in the near term, with cash marks continuing to rise against most European currencies.
He expects liquidation of long sterling/short mark positions to continue until the cash cross rate reaches 2.80.

September sterling futures were lower due to the cash cross activity, which was exacerbated by perceptions the Bank of England had finished raising U.K. rates. The BOE hiked rates by 1/4 point to 7.0 percent and signalled that rates have reached levels consistent with inflation targets.

"The fundamentals around the world have not changed," one futures trader said. "The U.S. won't raise rates, Germany can't afford to raise rates, and look what happened to sterling when the U.K. raised rates."
Mexican peso contracts widened losses amid active pit dealings, traders said. They said September pesos turned negative after hitting sell-stop orders near the daily high at $0.127000.
However, the contract held above support at $0.125000, and several traders now look for pesos to edge higher in the near term.
"There is really no reason for pesos to go lower," one trader said, noting that $0.0125000 was a key technical level. He said $0.128000 would be a strong resistance level.
Canadian dollars ended with marginal losses. One local firm bought 1,000 September contracts at about $0.7220 to the daily high of $0.7229, a pit trader said.
Other floor sources noted that September yen ended higher after absorbing moderately active selling earlier in the day. One French-based firm sold 2,000 contracts at $0.008490 to $0.008487.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was up $0.000016 at $0.008486, marks were up $0.0040 at $0.5367, Swiss francs were $0.0008 higher at $0.6562, sterling lost $0.0126 at $1.5858, Canadian dollars were off $0.0006 at $0.7220, Australian dollars were down $0.0061 at $0.7302 and Mexican pesos were off $0.000600 at $0.126075. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
